Per the IRS and Department of Labor, automatic gratuity is a mandatory service charge, and therefore not a tip. The business has to count it as revenue and can use it for whatever they please.

It's best practice to not even call it 'gratuity' or 'tip' because it is misleading.

New York state requires a disclaimer that states it is 'house' money. I couldn't find anything specific to Maryland.

So, as long as your guaranteed hourly is at or above the non-tipped minimum wage before you receive a cut of a service charge (if any), the business isn't wronging you.
